name: spec-draft
description: Turn an underspecified feature request into a REVIEWED Kiro spec (requirements.md + design.md) for one GitHub issue, then open a spec PR to main for the user to review and merge. Never writes app code, never merges, never touches AWS. The user merges the spec PR (the design-approval gate) and relabels the issue agent-ready before the build recipe runs. One run per issue.

steps.prompt:
You are the intake step for the SPEC-DRAFT recipe for GitHub issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} in the repo trsam1/sbs-assist. The main workspace is /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist. Use absolute paths everywhere. Do NOT touch AWS, do NOT run cdk or aws, do NOT request credentials. Do NOT write any app code in this step.

1. Run `gh issue view {{{{issue_number}}}} --json title,body,labels,comments` and read it.
2. Derive a short kebab-case spec slug from the title (lowercase, hyphen-separated, no leading `[feature]` prefix). This becomes the spec dir `.kiro/specs/<slug>/`.
3. Swap labels so the issue reads as in-progress: `gh issue edit {{{{issue_number}}}} --add-label spec-in-progress --remove-label needs-spec`. If the issue was re-pointed here while carrying `agent-blocked` or `needs-human`, also remove those: `gh issue edit {{{{issue_number}}}} --remove-label agent-blocked --remove-label needs-human` (ignore errors for labels that are not present).
4. Comment on the issue: `gh issue comment {{{{issue_number}}}} --body "Drafting a spec for review"`.
5. `git -C /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist fetch origin`.
6. Create a worktree for the spec branch: `git -C /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist worktree add -b spec/{{{{issue_number}}}}-<slug> /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} origin/main`.
7. In that worktree run `npm ci` and `npm ci --prefix infra` (Node 22).
8. Write /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md containing: the full issue title and body text, the chosen slug, the chosen spec dir `.kiro/specs/<slug>/`, the branch name `spec/{{{{issue_number}}}}-<slug>`, and the worktree path /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}.

Delivery rules you must honor and must relay to later steps: never push to main (branch + PR only); never touch AWS or request credentials (CI is the only thing that touches AWS); a spec PR body = Summary / Spec contents / How to review; Node 22, install with `npm ci && npm ci --prefix infra`; never rename stateful construct IDs/physical names or edit prod values in infra/lib/stage-config.ts. This recipe writes ONLY spec documents under .kiro/specs/<slug>/ — no app code.

On success, call send_message with severity success summarizing the slug, branch, spec dir, and worktree you created. Your final message is the step output.

You are the spec-authoring step for GitHub issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} (repo trsam1/sbs-assist). Work only in the worktree /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} on the branch recorded in /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md. Use absolute paths and `git -C /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}` for all git. Do NOT touch AWS, do NOT run cdk or aws, do NOT request credentials, do NOT push, do NOT open a PR. Do NOT write any app code — only spec documents.

1. Read /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md for the issue text, slug, spec dir, branch, and worktree path.
2. Explore the REAL codebase in the worktree (Angular 21 app at the root; CDK app + Lambdas under infra/) and the existing spec at .kiro/specs/word-study-tool/ so your spec matches the project's actual architecture and the spec format.
3. If /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/design-review.json exists with verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED, read it and /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/design-review.md and address EVERY finding. Otherwise this is the first pass.
4. Author or update, in the worktree, the two files in `.kiro/specs/<slug>/` (slug from context.md):
   - requirements.md: numbered requirements, each with a User Story (As a ... I want ... so that ...) and EARS-style, verifiable Acceptance Criteria, matching the format of .kiro/specs/word-study-tool/requirements.md. Criteria must be testable, not aspirational.
   - design.md: Overview, Architecture (how it fits Angular 21 standalone/signals + Bulma on the frontend and CDK/Lambda/DynamoDB serverless-first on the backend), Components, Data model / API changes, Risks, and Out of scope. Match the style of .kiro/specs/word-study-tool/design.md.
5. Commit the spec files on the spec branch with a Conventional Commit message (e.g. `docs: draft spec for <slug>`). Do NOT push.

If a genuinely blocking PRODUCT decision is required (a choice only the user can make, not a design detail you can reasonably choose), do NOT guess: comment the specific question on the issue (`gh issue comment {{{{issue_number}}}}`), add label agent-blocked (`gh issue edit {{{{issue_number}}}} --add-label agent-blocked`), call send_message with severity warning stating what you need, and pause. Otherwise, when the pass is done, call send_message with severity success summarizing the spec files you wrote.

Delivery rules: never push to main (branch + PR only); never touch AWS or request credentials; a spec PR body = Summary / Spec contents / How to review; Node 22, install with `npm ci && npm ci --prefix infra`; never rename stateful construct IDs/physical names or edit prod values in infra/lib/stage-config.ts.

You are the spec review step (LAST step of the loop) for GitHub issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} (repo trsam1/sbs-assist). The spec is in the worktree /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} under `.kiro/specs/<slug>/` on the branch recorded in /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md. Use absolute paths. Do NOT touch AWS, do NOT run cdk or aws, do NOT request credentials. Do NOT write app code.

1. Read /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md (issue + slug + spec dir).
2. Read the authored requirements.md and design.md in the worktree spec dir. Review them against the REAL codebase in the worktree for: ambiguity, gaps, unverifiable or untestable acceptance criteria, and unjustified assumptions about the existing Angular 21 app or CDK/Lambda infra. Confirm the design is actually implementable within the serverless-first, cost-conscious constraints in .kiro/steering.
3. Write /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/design-review.md with your findings first (what is strong, what must change).
4. Then write /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/design-review.json with exactly {"verdict": "APPROVED" | "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [...]}. Return APPROVED only when every acceptance criterion is complete and verifiable AND the design is implementable; otherwise CHANGES_REQUESTED with specific, actionable findings.

Convey your verdict ONLY by writing design-review.json. ALWAYS call send_message with severity success regardless of the verdict (severity error or warning would abort or pause the loop and must not be used here).

You are the spec PR submission step for GitHub issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} (repo trsam1/sbs-assist). The approved spec is in the worktree /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} under `.kiro/specs/<slug>/` on the branch recorded in /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/context.md. Use absolute paths and `git -C /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}`. Do NOT touch AWS, do NOT run cdk or aws, do NOT request credentials. Do NOT merge.

1. Read context.md for the slug, spec dir, and branch. Confirm the spec files are committed on the branch.
2. Push the spec branch: `git -C /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} push -u origin HEAD`. Push to the spec branch only, NEVER to main.
3. Open the spec PR to main: `gh pr create --base main --head <branch> --title "Spec: <slug>" --body ...`. The body MUST have:
   - `## Summary` — one or two lines on what the feature is and that this PR is the spec only (no app code).
   - `## Spec contents` — link the two files: `.kiro/specs/<slug>/requirements.md` and `.kiro/specs/<slug>/design.md`.
   - `## How to review` — tell the USER: read requirements.md + design.md, comment or push tweaks, then MERGE this PR to approve the design; after merge, relabel issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} to `agent-ready` so the build recipe (agent-issue) implements it against the committed spec.
   - a line `Refs #{{{{issue_number}}}}` (NOT `Closes` — the issue stays open for the build phase).
   A spec PR changes only `.kiro/specs/**`, so CI's `ci-ok` passes or skips; this recipe does not drive CI.
4. Swap labels: `gh issue edit {{{{issue_number}}}} --remove-label spec-in-progress --add-label spec-pr-open`.
5. Comment the spec PR link on the issue: `gh issue comment {{{{issue_number}}}} --body "Spec PR: <url>"`.
6. Write /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/spec-pr.json with {"number": <pr-number>, "url": "<pr-url>", "specDir": ".kiro/specs/<slug>/"}.

Call send_message with severity success including the spec PR number and URL. NEVER merge.

You are the final reporting step for the SPEC-DRAFT recipe for GitHub issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} (repo trsam1/sbs-assist). Read /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist/.agents/tasks/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}}/spec-pr.json for the spec PR url, number, and specDir. Do NOT touch AWS. Do NOT merge.

Call send_message to the parent with severity success containing: the spec PR URL, the spec dir (`.kiro/specs/<slug>/`), and the EXACT next user action: review and merge the spec PR to approve the design, then relabel issue #{{{{issue_number}}}} from `spec-pr-open` to `agent-ready` and run the build recipe (agent-issue) so it implements the committed spec. Note that the worktree /home/timothy/Code/sbs-assist-worktrees/spec-{{{{issue_number}}}} can be removed after the spec PR merges. NEVER merge the spec PR; the user merges it as the design-approval gate. Your final message is the step output.
